meta.title: Investor relations
meta.desc: Safe House Insurance is an independent bilingual agency on the Texas-New Mexico border, built around non-standard auto. Information for investors and an invitation to make contact.

hero.h1: The drivers everyone else declines are a market, not a leftover.
hero.lede:
Safe House Insurance is an independent agency on the Texas–New Mexico border, built
     around the customers the national carriers price out or turn away — non-standard auto,
     first-time and foreign licenses, SR-22 filings, lapsed coverage. It is a market that is
     underserved because it is harder to serve, and being harder to serve is exactly what keeps
     it defensible.

market.lead:
El Paso and Las Cruces sit on a border, and a border changes who needs
     insurance and how hard it is to write them.
market.p1:
A driver with a foreign license, a driver who crosses regularly, a household with one car and
     four names on it, a work truck that is also the family car — a national carrier's rating
     engine handles all of these badly, and a call centre handles them worse. Carriers disagree
     enormously about what these risks are worth, and that disagreement is the whole opportunity.
     It is why a single quote means nothing here and why an agency that can shop fourteen companies
     at once is worth more to the customer than any one of them.
market.p2:
It is also a market that does not attract competition easily. It takes appointments that
     carriers grant slowly, licenses in two states, and staff who can conduct the entire
     transaction in Spanish. None of those can be bought quickly.

built.lead: Not a plan. These exist today and can be verified.
built.carriers: carrier appointments, shopped on one form
built.years: combined years licensed, across the team
built.states: states licensed — Texas and New Mexico
built.pages: owned search pages, city by city

c1.p:
The agency represents a shelf of carriers rather than selling one company's product. That
         is the difference between competing on price against every other agent with the same
         product and competing on which company will write this particular person at all.

c2.h3: Bilingual as infrastructure, not as a feature
c2.p:
The whole transaction runs in Spanish when the customer wants it — the quote, the
         explanation of what a deductible does, the claim a year later. In this market that is not a
         marketing line, it is whether the business is reachable at all.

c3.p:
Agency revenue is commission on premium, and it renews. A policy placed once pays again at
         every renewal for as long as the client stays, and the cost of keeping them is service
         rather than acquisition. Growth compounds against a book that does not reset each year.

c4.h3: Demand we own rather than rent
c4.p:
The site answers the questions this market actually searches — what an SR-22 is, what
         happens after a lapse, what Texas requires, what to do with a foreign license — city
         by city across both states. That is inbound that does not stop when an ad budget does.

money.p1:
An independent agency earns a commission on the premium it places, paid by the carrier, and
     earns it again at each renewal. There is no underwriting risk on the agency's balance sheet:
     the carrier takes the claim. What the agency owns is the relationship and the book.
money.p2:
That makes the economics legible. Growth comes from three places — more policies, more
     lines per household, and keeping the ones already placed — and each of those is
     measurable and improvable independently.

contact.lead:
If you invest in agencies, brokerages or local financial services and this is the
     kind of business you look at, we would rather talk than send a deck into the dark.
contact.p: Write to {email} with a line about who you are and what you look for, or call {call} during office hours. Financial detail is shared directly, under a mutual NDA, with people whose interest is real — not published on a web page.
